title: A Figure Held Edge-On

arc.title: The Cold Stone
arc.subtitle: a warm stone, already going cold

epigraph.text: At the first counting of the firing month the crier holds the slate edge-on to his own forearm and reads a figure the goers-by cannot see. An arm come down from the Weir knows the weight of what it carried and not what it cost; a hand going to a slate knows the figure before it knows the face. The yard keeps what it keeps in wood, cord and wool, and a thing set where nobody looks is a thing nobody can be made to give back.
epigraph.attribution: A saying of the moot-post, spoken at the first Account-day of Tallow

where: Low Kiln, the Weir and Sill
pov: Daniel Marchetti (Corin), close third-person past tense inside a one-hundred-and-fifty-three-to-one-hundred-and-fifty-nine-day-old body carried everywhere, told by nobody; the surgeon's register colours the noticing (the firing read as a theatre he cannot enter, the kiln's breath as a danger behind a screen, the carrying arm as a record in muscle that keeps weight and not cost, the slate held edge-on as a figure that arrives nowhere, a slate-runner's hand to slate before eye as an eighth record-first shape on a place of its own) without a present-tense Chicago break or a tagged remembered line --- the old life stays offstage --- and there is no departure from his eyes, no Court, collector, back-room interior, Marra in Sill, tenth stopping, seventh hearing, calling of the loan, spending of the seventh year or ending; the foundling stays offstage, the green is never Fenna in narration, and no name, figure or payer is given to any withholding

scenes.title: The Second Working Morning
scenes.synopsis: First entry, first dated heading and drop capital of the chapter: Day 153, Tallow 4, Fourthday, before first grey through the morning under the Vail kiln-house roof and at the kiln mouth. The boy is one hundred and fifty-three days old and five months and three days and nobody under any roof says so (T071/T072). The widow's mark hangs where it hung, untouched since the kiln mouth on Day 150 and not to be touched at a shelf, a well, an afternoon or a dusk; Sella feeds the fire under the back of a broken pot and it answers four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for a hundred and fifty-three days (T058/T079, T088). The first smell is hot clay under tallow and the first sound the kiln's breath with its gap, not a bell; the Cross is silent until Tallow 10. The yard goes around the clean dark line, the finer grey called the thaw, the rack space with its broken birth-slates and the missing hand's place with a look and a wide step and no number; the trough by the well stands bare and dark and the clay jar stands cold under its glaze (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried). No collector comes; Tarn takes the broom only after it is instructed, his seventh year still held with six counted where the house can check, and the nine stoppings remain nine with no tenth stood up and the loan uncalled (T036/T076, T061/T082). The boy reads an opening as a thing done and gone past, a theatre with the danger behind a screen and a cost paid by a man whose name is not spoken (T062). Advances T071/T072 (153 exact), T088, T058/T079, T009/T013/T092, T098, T036/T076, T061/T082 and T062.

scenes.title: Dust Ground Small as Meal
scenes.synopsis: Second entry and dated heading of Day 154, Tallow 5, Fifthday, before first grey into the morning at the Vail wheel-shed, the flagstones and the edge of the worked strips. The firing season gathers: three or four unnamed men go low-voiced into the finger's-width-open back room and Sella carries past at the half-pace, gives the house no name for them and does not say the room is cold. Jorra comes through with fine grey slate dust ground small as meal into both forearms past the bent little finger and under the nails, not bone-coloured slip; he keeps dusty forearms and clean ones on one tray, speaks to the wheel before anyone (It doesn't care whose hands. It cares if they're steady), tells a pot You'll do, knows its full note before it leaves the wheel and withholds the knowing from a High Kiln kiln-master who says the pot is singing before its time and that such a pot generally sings itself out early (T035/T031, T061/T082). Before Sella has finished telling him the fire is low his bent finger goes into the cold damper, moves the tongue a hair's breadth and leaves it standing; the boy reads one iron with two bites, the holding and the taking, filed joined to no kiln (T062). Tarn's stroke goes on over the flagstones past the shallow bright patch without the half-check while the stones keep the place where it stopped, and neither man asks about the ear or the room (T036/T076). No third telling of the shut counting room comes; the two tellings stay side by side with no joining (T065/T095). Under the roof the pan's gone place and the shelf's two gaps stay on separate trays, the fold keeps one stiff crust and its empty place, the field's empty place is gone around, no third gap comes and no fourth likeness is made a cause (T060/T086, T097, T098). The charcoal under the board waits unread (T100). Advances T035/T031, T062, T061/T082, T065/T095, T036/T076, T060/T086, T097, T100 and T071/T072 (154 exact).

scenes.title: What the Arm Knows
scenes.synopsis: Third entry and dated heading of Day 155, Tallow 6, Sixthday, morning into afternoon downriver at the Weir: the plank walk on posts, the flat blessing stone, the lower boards, the fish-trade shade below the sill and the out-of-line landing below the north bridge. The last reed work is finished and has become a direction rather than a bundle: the going down and the coming back are counted in the arm that carries them, and a cost asked as a direction is answered with the river and the weather, leaving no entry (T071/T072, T077). Sella sets the basket at the edge of the work where no slate lies and gives the instruction to the wool and the running water and never to the basket (T058/T079). The reed-cutter's grey cord goes straightened and turned on the blessing stone, one knot tied low with teeth and bitten off and put back inside his coat with the flat of the hand, the knots unread (T099 carried, not paid). Orra Weir, hands like old rope, pale eel scars uncovered, salt white at her wrists, the nasal half-song of the Fen in her voice where she is tired, pulls one knot down and gives a date where a figure is asked --- the ninth of Ilmen, the collector's boat round the bend on the flood with six oars and one man at the stern who never touched them --- and the forty-first double turn stays legible, tail tucked, left over right with the weight of a thumb, while the word forty is unspoken (T024/T059/T025). Mira Silt answers a thin run with Thin? Who's to say thin? It comes when it comes. Ask the river, flicks eel-bones while deciding whether to lie, shows the second twist twice beneath her apron with neither knot counted and her board beside Orra's and not touching (T059/T025). Below the sill a child's foot stays dark in three turns of wool, the cold to one woman and weather to the yard (T093/T094/T096); the soft-cuffed clerk stays set at the landing with his slate turned inward, hand to slate before eyes to stalls, for a measure nobody called (T090/T080). The foundling stays offstage: the sixth glimpse has landed and is not spent for effect (T033/T034). Advances T071/T072 (155 exact), T077, T058/T079, T099, T024/T059/T025, T093/T094/T096, T090/T080 and T033/T034.

scenes.title: The Man in Mud End
scenes.synopsis: Fourth entry and dated heading of Day 156, Tallow 7, Seventhday, morning through the going of the light at the Clay Yard, the yard well, the drying racks and under the Vail roof. The kiln's breath becomes a named danger in the yard without being made a lesson: a woman raking the mouth speaks sideways of a man in Mud End taken in his sleep, quiet as a lamb, and them that found him called it merciful; nobody makes a lesson of it and nobody puts a figure to him, and the district goes on with the work (T088). The boy reads it the way he once read a danger behind a screen in a theatre he could not enter --- heat kept and counted, a gate with two bites, the almost-smile that is not peace and the knowing worth nothing with the heat two paces off --- and no payer is named to the silence (T062, T088). At the trough whose skin of ice has gone the water stands bare and dark and is called weather; at the well a woman letting down the bucket says the water tastes different and another says weather, and the argument ends where such arguments end (T058/T079). The yard goes around the clean dark line, the new finer grey called the thaw, the space beneath the lowest rack where the broken birth-slates lie and the empty place in the returning line where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out --- a look and a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried). At the going of the light Sella sets the boy on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without looking at his face, leaves the thread of drool frozen and unwiped, tells the fire it was the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it, counts under her breath toward no opening, sets the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand, does not touch the widow's mark because a dusk is not an opening, and goes to her own bed; the two rooms do not touch (T058/T079, T088). The fire gives four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for a hundred and fifty-six days. Advances T071/T072 (156 exact), T088, T058/T079, T062, T009/T013/T092 and T098.

scenes.title: Beneath the Front Edge
scenes.synopsis: Fifth entry and dated heading of Day 157, Tallow 8, Eighthday, morning into the going of the light under the Vail kiln-house roof at the loaf shelf seen from the basket's low angle and the hearth. The household's arithmetic stays in loaves pushed along a board, a glance at the clay jar cold under its glaze and a space at the row's end nobody calls a number; a neighbour with wet sleeves asks what the firing costs set down there and is sent to the pot with Ask the pot what a wet thing costs set down there. The house has said it, and carries the unanswered question away level so nothing slops (T077). Standing with her back to the basket and moving her lips along the row, Sella reaches a finger BENEATH the front edge where the charcoal tally lies, without looking and without a word, brings it away and does not go back to the shelf; the boy sees the hand go under and come back and sees nothing of what the marks say, for such a hand either knows the board by heart or has been told not to look, and the reason stands between the two (T100 carried, unread). The shelf keeps two unnamed gaps, no third comes, and the stiff brown-edged crust lies two inches from his ear with its empty place beside it still unnamed and no third (T060/T086, T097). The pan's gone place keeps the round shape of its absence on a place of its own and is not laid across the shelf's gaps, the fold's crust, the field's empty place, the sixth colour or the sixth shape (T097, T050/T051, T033/T034). At the hearth she tells the fire it was the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it, stands a moment counting under her breath toward no opening, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist, the grey streak pale off the coals, sets the pot rim out with its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand and does not look toward the bed; the fire gives four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for a hundred and fifty-seven days (T088, T058/T079). Advances T100, T060/T086, T097, T077, T058/T079, T088, T050/T051, T033/T034 and T071/T072 (157 exact).

scenes.title: A Direction Up the Clay Road
scenes.synopsis: Sixth entry and dated heading of Day 158, Tallow 9, Ninthday, the eve of the Account-day, morning at the Clay Yard and the wheel-shed edge and afternoon under the Vail roof. Berr's red wool cord of office folded square under his coat is spoken of as a direction up the clay road toward High Kiln, not as a place anybody means to go that day; a number comes up from the road in a man's fist and goes toward the block and arrives nowhere, passed from fist to mouth to shoulder while the printed one in twelve stands unchallenged until the reading (T015/T041/T047, T077). **The chapter's one meaningful change is planted here:** Hessa Rale, a slate-runner from Slate Row who carries Berr's narrow slate between the Cross and Greybank, comes through the yard with the slate held edge-on to her own forearm, her hand going to it before her eyes go to the people in the yard; she is given a full sheet before her first line of dialogue and filed as an eighth record-first hand-shape on a place of its own, not joined to Marra, the Court-table clerk, the Fishstairs clerk, the soft-handed man from Slate Row, the twice-wiped thumb or the charcoal under the shelf (T080, advanced and not paid). She is a runner, not a reader of any private keeping; no figure is read from her slate and no joining is made. Tarn's seventh year is pressed nearer its end and still held, the small knife at the very edge of its sill with six counted where the house can check and the seventh where it cannot, the unforged collector sentence beside it, the Seed 16 breath unspent and the loan uncalled; no tenth stopping stands up (T036/T076, T061/T082). Jorra's dust and the bent finger at the damper go unasked about, the two silences stay unjoined, and the boy is one hundred and fifty-eight days old and nobody says so (T035/T031, T062, T071/T072). Advances T015/T041/T047, T077, T080, T036/T076, T061/T082, T035/T031, T062, T058/T079 and T071/T072 (158 exact).

scenes.title: One in Twelve, As the Notice Says
scenes.synopsis: Seventh entry, dated heading and chapter close: Day 159, Tallow 10, Tenthday, the first Account-day and market-day of Tallow, morning at the Cross up to the reading block under the moot-post and the going of the light on the clay road home. Berr Clay comes up short off the clay road with the red wool cord of his office folded square under his coat and the green of tasted lead glaze at one mouth-corner, wipes his thumb twice before touching nothing, holds a narrow slate unopened to his forearm, passes a finger over the figure, reads one in twelve, as the notice says low into the goers-by, calls the levy and denies it with your house, never I, and goes off toward High Kiln with the box locked and the true subtraction inside, believing he has done a kindness --- the figure read still not the figure paid (T015/T041/T047, T077). The heard bell stands beside the told bell, four, four and a gap, with nobody crossing himself (T078). Hessa Rale is seen again taking the narrow slate up the clay road toward Greybank, hand to slate before eye to the crowd, the eighth record-first shape on its own place and joined to none (T080, advanced, not paid); the soft-cuffed clerk stays at the out-of-line landing below the north bridge with his slate turned inward, hand to slate before eyes to stalls, for a measure nobody called (T090/T080). Sella sets the basket in the moot-post's finger's width of shade where no slate lies, keeps the half-pace from every open slate and carries him home at the going of the light saying nothing (T058/T079). In the small hours under the Vail roof the file is exact, complete and worthless: six hearings beside and never among with no seventh, three near-full answers advanced and not paid, nine stoppings with no payer named to any and no tenth before the seventh year is earned, one stiff crust and its empty place, two shelf gaps, the pan's gone place, a sixth colour and a sixth shape on places of their own, the loan uncalled and the Seed 16 breath unspent (T061/T082, T036/T076, T060/T086, T097, T050/T051, T033/T034). One hundred and fifty-nine stands exact and unspent as his hand goes up an inch toward the note of water over water and comes down against the fold, and the carried fire misses its fifth under the floor with its payer unnamed for a hundred and fifty-nine days (T071/T072, T088). Nothing joined, paid, named, opened, called or ended; the chapter pulls forward into Day 160, Tallow 11, and the working season deepening. Advances T015/T041/T047, T077, T078, T080, T090, T058/T079, T061/T082, T036/T076, T060/T086, T097, T050/T051, T033/T034, T071/T072 (159 exact) and T088.
